h.about.label: About us
h.about.p0: Faina Polyana was founded in 2015, when several family farms from villages of the Ternopil region decided to work together under the classic European cooperative model.
h.about.p1: The idea was simple: a small grower alone cannot guarantee a buyer volumes, consistent quality or certification. A hundred growers with shared standards, their own facilities and one quality control system can.
h.about.p2: Today the cooperative unites 153 producers from ten communities in the Ternopil and Ivano-Frankivsk regions. Each member grows berries on their own land, while the cooperative handles intake, cooling, freezing, sorting, storage, logistics and sales.
h.about.p3: In 2018 we built Ukraine's first cooperative berry-freezing facility. The cooperative bought the site with its own funds, recently completed a new 650 m² frozen-berry warehouse and is already preparing the next stage of expansion.
h.about.title: A cooperative built on trust
h.adv0.d: Raw material comes from over 100 ha of members' plantations and from trusted growers in neighbouring regions. A poor harvest on one farm never puts a contract at risk.
h.adv1.d: We know which plot, which grower and which day every berry came from — all the way to your warehouse.
h.adv2.d: Members work with the cooperative's agronomists, so quality is built in on the plantation.
h.adv3.d: Members who take payment at the end of the season receive a 50% premium, so delivering the best berries pays off for everyone.
h.adv4.d: All processing is done in-house and the contract is directly with you: a fair price, transparent origin and direct responsibility for quality.
h.geo.label: Geography
h.geo.p: Collection points are located right in the communities where berries are grown. From there the fruit quickly reaches the central hub in Horodyshche near Ternopil.
h.geo.pts: 12 points: Kozova, Berezhany, Pidhaitsi, Zboriv, Zbarazh, Terebovlia, Buchach, Chortkiv, Monastyryska, Rohatyn, Burshtyn, Halych

p.ben.label: Benefits
p.ben.title: What partners get
p.ben0.d: You buy berries directly from those who grew them: no resellers, no extra mark-ups and no lost information about origin.
p.ben1.d: Agronomic support, intake close to the plantations, IQF and A/B grading: every lot meets the agreed specification.
p.ben2.d: On request we provide data for every lot: grower, intake date, freezing date and lot number.
p.ben3.d: 10 kg cartons with food-grade liners, 300 g – 1 kg retail packs, private label; minimum order from 20 t.
p.ben4.d: A supply base of 153 farms and 300 t of cold storage let us plan deliveries all year round.
p.ben5.d: Certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate, laboratory reports and lot specification.

p.inv0.d: Co-financing the “Horodyshche 2028” programme: a second IQF tunnel, optical sorting, a logistics centre and 1,000 t of cold storage.

p.inv2.d: Joint projects with donor programmes: cooperative development, grower training, energy independence.
p.inv3.d: Taking part in international tenders for frozen berry supply with a full set of documents and certificates.
p.org.alt: Participants of the “Power of Cooperatives” forum
p.org.label: How we are organised
p.org.p0: Faina Polyana is an agricultural cooperative founded in 2015 on the classic European model. Each member owns their land and co-owns the shared facilities.
p.org.p1: Growers care about quality because they share in the added value; decisions are made collectively and transparently, and stability is built into the model — the cooperative does not depend on a single owner.

pl.hub.p1: The “Horodyshche 2028” modernisation programme will raise freezing capacity to 30 t per day, storage to 1,000 t and processing to 1,500 t per season by 2028.
